infoDescription: Ornitho2eBird converts exports from ornitho, Observation and BirdLasser into eBird-ready checklists.
infoHowItWorksIntro: eBird only collects lists, so all imported observations must be converted to eBird checklists. The tool handles imported lists and casual observations differently.
infoHowItWorksChecklistIntro: Collecting data as lists on ornitho (complete or not) makes conversion to eBird much easier and is therefore strongly recommended.
infoHowItWorksChecklistPointOne: Easy conversion into eBird checklists because almost all metadata is already available.
infoHowItWorksChecklistPointTwo: Using the track in Naturalist is strongly recommended so checklist distance can be carried over automatically. Without distance, checklists become historical in eBird.
infoHowItWorksChecklistPointThree: Number of observers is not recorded in ornitho, so the app uses the default value defined in Settings.
infoHowItWorksChecklistPointFour: The app assumes that if you submitted a list, birding was the primary purpose.
infoHowItWorksSightingsIntro: Casual observations need to be aggregated into checklists before export.
infoHowItWorksSightingsPointOne: The app uses an automatic aggregation based on time and distance parameters (see below for details).
infoHowItWorksSightingsPointThree: Birding is not assumed to be the primary purpose for these checklists, so they are not marked as primary purpose by default.
infoHowItWorksSightingsPointFour: These checklists are not considered complete by default.
infoAutoAssignTitle: How does the aggregation of casual observation work?
infoAutoAssignIntro: The tool automatically groups casual observations into new checklists based on distance and time parameters (see settings).
infoAutoAssignPointTwo: The first casual observation becomes the seed of a new checklist. Later casual observations are added to that checklist when they occur on the same calendar day and fall within both the distance and duration thresholds of at least one observation already in the checklist. Otherwise, they start a new checklist. Aggregation never spans midnight.
infoAutoAssignPointThree: Grouping is transitive: if A matches B and B matches C, all three can end up in the same checklist.
infoAutoAssignPointFour: Aggregation creates new checklists only. It does not add casual observations to existing checklists.
infoAutoAssignPointFive: If no time is available, the casual observation is treated as 00:00. With the default 24-hour duration threshold, same-day aggregation is therefore driven mainly by distance.
infoAutoAssignPointSix: The duration and distance thresholds can be adjusted in Settings.
infoCustomizeTitle: How to manually customize your checklist?
infoCustomizeBody: Turn on Customized mode in Settings to manually assign casual observations to checklists and edit checklist metadata before export, including primary purpose, protocol, date, time, duration, distance, observers, location and checklist comments.
infoCustomizeSpeciesComments: You can also modify species comments. Use the template settings to decide what information is added to each eBird species comment, such as count, time, links to the source observation, map links and original notes.
introWorkflowImport: Export the data you want to import from the source website, for example ornitho.ch.
introWorkflowExport: Download the eBird Record Format CSV generated by the app.
introWorkflowEbirdImport: Go to the eBird import page and upload the CSV.
introWorkflowReview: After import, review checklist locations, hotspot matches and species names in eBird.
prerequisiteLabel: Before continuing, confirm that you understand:
importantRuleOne: Mapping protocols from ornitho, BirdLasser or Observation to eBird is not always exact. Complete stationary or traveling checklists are preferred when you can provide effort details.
importantRuleTwo: Keeping a link to the source observation in species comments can help eBird reviewers validate records.
importantRuleThree: For pre-eBird life list imports that do not meet current eBird checklist rules, consolidate data carefully and review the import afterward.
